  • run_stochastic(s) consumes the stoch_* fields (scenario count stoch_S ∈ [3,5], probability vector, held-out budget stoch_H_oos) and solves the two-stage extensive-form welfare over seeded scenarios — nonanticipativity-tied battery first stage, per-scenario exactness gates, per-scenario probability-de-scaled DADPs as the price output — then evaluates the fixed first stage out-of-sample on held-out draws from a disjoint sub-seed family.

For the ordinary :centralized/:admm strategies these field blocks are no-ops — adding them changed the savename string (a documented, accepted cost) but not a single existing numeric result.

Where it lives: src/experiments/Scenario.jl (spec + construction validation), materialize.jl (sub_seed, build_feeder/ build_price/build_population), run.jl (run_scenario, ScenarioResult), store.jl (run_and_store, scenario_filename), sweep.jl (run_sweep, collate_summary), mpc_loop.jl and run_stochastic.jl (the independent entry points); editable script mirrors under scripts/run_scenario.jl and scripts/sweep.jl.
See it run: "The Experiment Harness" docs page (all three figures above are its live outputs), plus "Rung 8: MPC / Rolling-Horizon RTP" and "Rung 9: Stochastic PV/Demand Uncertainty" for the two independent entry points.

How the Framework Earns Trust

A framework whose product is prices read off duals has an unusual failure mode: almost nothing that goes wrong produces a solver error. A slack relaxation, a sign-flipped dual convention, a silently drifted regression — all return plausible-looking numbers. The validation philosophy here is therefore structural, not aspirational: every claim is guarded by a certificate, an independent oracle, or a pinned regression, and the guards refuse or report rather than massage.

Certificates: refuse a price before returning a wrong one

The headline gate is assert_socp_exact!. After every trusted SOCP solve it computes the per-branch, per-hour cone residual \( \big|\, \ell_{ij}[t]\, v_i[t] - (P_{ij}[t]^2 + Q_{ij}[t]^2) \,\big| \) against a scale-free threshold, and on failure it throws, refusing to return any price: a strict cone at the optimum means \(\ell\) is a fictitious over-current and the DADP duals are physically meaningless — with no solver error to warn you. The maximum gap is also a first-class output (exact_maxgap) on every ScenarioResult, so exactness is something a reader can check on every published number. The same certificate discipline recurs throughout: the reactive dual is only extracted behind an assert_no_slack gate, the overvoltage-capable restricted formulation carries its own AC-feasibility certificate (assert_restriction_exact!), and the meshed rung's angle-recoverability certificate downgrades an unrecoverable solve to an honest upper bound on welfare instead of a claimed optimum.

Independent oracles: cross-examination, not self-grading

  • The AC-exactness oracle. An oracle that re-solved the same relaxed cone would prove nothing, so ACPowerFlow is a genuinely independent nonconvex peer: the true equality \(\ell_{ij} v_i = P_{ij}^2 + Q_{ij}^2\), solved by Ipopt through the same unchanged solve_welfare seam. assert_ac_exact! certifies the SOCP solution against it per hour — and deliberately reports rather than throws, because a genuine gap is a finding, not a defect to suppress.
  • Cross-strategy and cross-formulation validation. ADMM is cross-validated against the centralized optimum on both IEEE-13 (congestion-binding) and IEEE-123 (voltage-binding) feeders; a conformance test proves the DC ↔ LinDistFlow swap changes one argument and no results on a loss-less fixture. (The design also reserves PowerModels/PowerModelsDistribution as an external data-parsing and formulation oracle, but it is deliberately kept out of the runtime dependencies; the shipped certifications rest on the independent Ipopt AC peer, closed-form fixtures, and the MPEC oracle below.)
  • BilevelJuMP 4-way certification of the planning layer. The planning game's most dangerous ambiguities are interpretive — which agent is the leader, and what sign convention the coupling dual \(\pi[t]\) carries (the source note itself labels the roles inconsistently once). On a small instance, four independent routes must agree: BilevelJuMP's StrongDualityMode MPEC reduction, its ProductMode reduction, brute-force hand enumeration, and the production hand-rolled Benders loop. They do (same \(z^*\), \(x_{inv}^*\), and cost), and the agreement is retained as a permanent regression — the role and sign conventions are empirically certified, not assumed.

Pinned golden regressions, gated before pinned

Numeric results that matter are pinned as goldens under a gate-then-golden discipline: the validity gates (exactness, convergence, certificate status) are asserted first, and only then is the pinned value compared — so a golden can never quietly enshrine an invalid solve. The ~2,800-test suite also carries guards that defend scope decisions mechanically: an automated no-binaries guard with a source-level tripwire over every planning-layer subproblem builder (negative-tested — the guard is proven to fire), a known solver incapacity pinned as an asserted negative regression, and acceptance gates over the end-to-end IEEE-13/123 runs.

The honest-reporting culture

The most distinctive validation choice is cultural, and it is encoded in code rather than prose:

  • Thesis reproduction is labeled directional-only. On real public IEEE-123 data, the thesis's qualitative headline reproduces: switching from a flat feed-in tariff to DADP pricing flips the DSO surplus from negative to positive. The quantitative headline does not: the thesis's +25% welfare gain shows up here as roughly +0.045%, and the sign flip itself is knife-edge fragile under a ±2–5% population perturbation. Every reproduced number carries the fixed "directional, public-data" qualifier, the golden is pinned on the sign-safe quantity only, and the assumptions page even publishes corrections against its own earlier claims (a reported exactness failure that turned out to be a solver-tolerance artifact is struck through and re-measured, not silently edited away).
  • Nash results are "a" converged equilibrium, never "the". Gauss–Seidel diagonalization carries no uniqueness guarantee, so the honesty gate is structural: run_nash_probe re-solves from at least 3 seeds and 2 sweep orders and reports the spread across converged points. The never-"the" language is produced by the reporting code itself.
  • Negative findings ship as findings. The AC oracle surfaced that the SOC relaxation is genuinely inexact under high-PV reverse flow — the thesis's own motivating scenario — and the framework published the boundary (applicability maps), refused to price the regime, and then built a dedicated formulation for it, keeping the failed simpler alternative documented as a citable negative result.

The net effect: when this framework returns a price, a welfare number, or an equilibrium, that number has survived a certificate, at least one independent peer, and a pinned regression — and where it could not survive one, the framework says so in the result itself.
